data.name: Zachian
data.gender_notes: Zachian is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name 'Zacharias' and the Greek name 'Zacharias', which both mean 'God remembers'. In the Bible, Zacharias was a priest who was visited by the angel Gabriel and told that his wife would give birth to a son named John. This miraculous event reminded the Jewish people of God's promises and His faithfulness to remember His covenant.
data.etymology: Zachian belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God remembers.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Zachian total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_greek.name: Ζαχιαν

in_english.name: Zachian
in_english.long_meaning: The name Zachian is derived from Hebrew roots, meaning 'God remembers' or 'remembered by God'. This name is linked to the biblical tradition, echoing the significance of remembrance and divine recollection in Christian theology. It symbolizes the enduring memory of God and His covenant with humanity.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Zachian' carries a rich heritage from the Jewish and Christian traditions, as it is derived from the biblical names 'Zacharias'. This name may serve as a reminder of the miraculous birth of John the Baptist, and may be passed down through generations to preserve this historical and cultural significance.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Zachian' holds spiritual significance as it is a reminder of God's promises and His faithfulness to remember His covenant. It is a name that encourages trust and faith in God's provision and sovereignty, and may serve as a source of inspiration and courage for those who bear the name. Additionally, it is a name that points to the importance of remembering the past and cherishing God's promises in the present and future.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Zachary means "God remembers." This name symbolizes God's faithfulness and memory in the lives of those who bear this name. It is a reminder of God's promise to never forget His people and to always be present in their lives.

historical_references.reference: Zacharias, a Hebrew priest, was the father of John the Baptist. Luke 1:5-25 describes how Zacharias, unbelieving, was struck mute by the angel Gabriel until the child's birth when his speech was restored.
historical_references.context: Ancient Israel, around the time of the Second Temple, before the birth of John the Baptist and Jesus Christ.

historical_references.reference: Saint Zacharius of Mytilene, a bishop and martyr, was persecuted under emperor Diocletian for his faith. He was tortured, had his limbs severed, and was ultimately executed in 304 AD.
